chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said: My father related to me that Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il ibn Bazigh, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir that Abu Ja`far (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, the One – may His Names be Blessed and Exalted in His Elevated Essence – united everything in His Unity, then applied it to His Creation. Therefore, He is Alone, the Needless, the Master, and the glorified. Everything serves Him, and everything depends upon Him. Our Lord is beyond our grasp, and our Lord’s Knowledge encompasses everything.

key_terms.يَصْمِدُ إِلَيْهِ: depends upon Him / turns to Him

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about Allah's Unity and Knowledge?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the transition of Divine Unity from its absolute, incomprehensible essence (*fi kenuhi*) to its manifestation in creation, describing Allah as *Ahad* (Unique) and *Samad* (Eternal Refuge). The text highlights that while all entities worship and depend upon Him, His essence remains transcendent beyond human reach, yet His knowledge is all-encompassing. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on distinguishing between Allah's essence and His attributes, affirming both His transcendence and immanence in creation.
